figures.title: Nonblinking fractions and volume
figures.summary: The four core families are 2.2 nm (black), 3.0 nm (red), 4.0 nm (green) and 5.5 nm (blue). Panel a plots the nonblinking fraction against shell monolayers; panel b contrasts large- and small-core on-time histograms; panel c relates the fraction to average particle volume. The approximate 750 nm³ threshold and graphical uncertainty bars are retained without digitizing new precision. The caption uses at least 99% on-time, while main prose elsewhere uses greater than 99%.

figures.title: Lifetime versus volume
figures.summary: Average photoluminescence lifetimes are plotted against total particle volume for the same four core-size families. Most series approach roughly 65 ns above approximately 750 nm³, but the 3.0 nm series continues to increase. The reported SI table provides its fitted values; the plotted trend is not a universal lifetime rule.

intuition.summary: Estimate required shell material from core concentration, core size and successive shell volume increments, assuming complete precursor conversion and one monolayer equal to half the wurtzite c parameter. These assumptions do not constitute measured lattice constants or atomic coordinates.

intuition.title: Ligand steric interpretation
intuition.summary: The authors speculate that the secondary amine functions as a base but is disfavored as a thick-shell bound ligand by steric crowding. Surface flattening favors oleate. Figure S5 is a conceptual packing drawing; its branched descriptor refers to the secondary-amine architecture, not an identified carbon-chain isomer.

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Prospects of Colloidal Nanocrystals for Electronic and Optoelectronic Applications

general_background.title: Solvent and transport
general_background.summary: A solvent carries dissolved species and transports heat through a reaction or dispersion. Solubility, viscosity and molecular interactions affect how precursors and ligand-coated particles move and mix.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
